$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the internal bridge RESPONSE envelope shape (BridgeResp). Mirrors extension/src/shared/types.ts:BridgeResp; keep the two in sync (types.ts is not generated from this yet). `error` is the extension-side free-text reason and `code` its optional classification from contracts/errors.json -- the extension names the failures it can (see shared/bridge-error.ts), and the Rust side allowlists what it accepts and falls back to EXECUTION_FAILED. Transport-level codes (NOT_CONNECTED, RESPONSE_TIMEOUT, CONNECTION_LOST) are still assigned Rust-side and never travel on this envelope. RESERVED ID: a frame with id 0 is the extension's ANNOUNCE, not a reply -- see the `id` property below.
title: BridgeResp
description: The response posted back from the extension to the native host over the Port. Shape: { id, ok, data?, error?, code? }.

id.description: Correlation id, echoed from the matching BridgeReq. The value 0 is RESERVED and never a request id (the server's counter starts at 1): a frame with id 0 carrying `data.announce` is the extension's version announce, sent unsolicited right after connecting. It wears this envelope deliberately, so that a server predating the announce still parses it (an undeserializable line would kill its reader loop and drop the connection) and merely logs an unroutable id. See extension/src/shared/announce.ts and src/peer.rs.

ok.description: Whether the op succeeded. When false, `error` carries a human-readable reason.

data.description: The op's payload on success. Shape varies per op; intentionally unconstrained (`unknown` in types.ts).

error.description: Human-readable failure reason when ok is false. Always present on a failure; `code` is the machine-readable companion and may be absent.

code.description: Optional stable taxonomy code from contracts/errors.json, set when the extension can name the failure (TAB_NOT_FOUND, UNSUPPORTED_PAGE, EXTENSION_NOT_READY, TOOL_DISABLED). Absent means unclassified, which the server reports as EXECUTION_FAILED -- the honest answer for 'the op ran and failed'. An unrecognised value degrades the same way rather than being passed through, so a typo cannot invent taxonomy.
